Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-15 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Ramirez (Redwood SE), Lena Cho (Horizon Eng Mgr), Tom Nguyen (Horizon DevOps), Priya Kapoor (Product), Aaron Feld (Security)

Summary (auto): weekly pilot check-in, focus on access & infra gating, quick benchmark readout, security asks.

--- Transcript Start ---
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, we'll kick off. can you hear me okay?
[00:04] Lena Cho: yep, we can hear you. good to go.
[00:08] Maya Patel: cool. quick agenda — access status, short bench readout from staging, SLO alignment and then security blockers. carlos will cover the latency numbers.
[00:16] Carlos Ramirez: hi all, dropping in. i ran the 500-sample and a 1k sample yesterday, will summarise the tails and why cache warmup matters.
[00:24] Tom Nguyen: before we start, quick note — peering request is in, but there was a CIDR overlap on our side, so we refiled. should be resolved by EOD tomorrow, just FYI.
[00:33] Maya Patel: good heads up tom, thanks. lena, anything new from product side?
[00:36] Lena Cho: we're mostly aligned; priya's here to talk success criteria — we care about p95 < 220ms for short prompts, and operational cost per 1k requests target is in our doc.
[00:44] Priya Kapoor: yeah, i just want to avoid surprises — tail latency spikes are our biggest risk. also we need a defined rollback plan for canary.
[00:52] Carlos Ramirez: noted. quick bench notes: staging runs used Redwood hosted small cluster, synthetic prompt mix skewed to 40-60 tokens and some long context. median was ~95ms, p95 ~210ms, p99 ~560ms on cold cache. with prefix cache warm (kv cache warmed) p99 drops to ~310ms.
[01:10] Aaron Feld: 560ms p99 cold, okay that's higher than we'd like but acceptable for pilot. question on encryption — are logs forwarded plain or redacted by default?
[01:18] Maya Patel: logs are redacted by default, we can provide audit logs with KMS-wrapped keys. for private deployments audit streams can be sent to customer s3 or syslog.
[01:28] Tom Nguyen: about keys — our security team requires KMS and optional HSM. is HSM supported in private on prem?
[01:35] Carlos Ramirez: we support KMS integrations for private. HSM on-prem is something we can discuss with infra team; there may be additional ops work.
[01:42] Lena Cho: and SSO? our corp idp is okta, we need SAML SSO for console access and SSO-auto onboarding for devs.
[01:49] Maya Patel: yes, SAML/SSO is standard, we can share the SSO metadata and a checklist. we'll include it in the handoff doc.
[01:55] Priya Kapoor: can we also get a short doc on exploded costs — i.e. how batching and quantization affect unit cost? our finance team will ask.
[02:04] Maya Patel: absolutely. we'll include Redwood Optimize suggestions — e.g., how a mix of batching + 4-bit quant can reduce token cost by X% (we'll provide numbers from a similar pilot).
[02:12] Carlos Ramirez: back to benchmarks, there's an important nuance: sequence length distribution. when we feed longer context samples (800+ tokens), p99 climbs a lot — in that workload we hit ~720ms p99 even warm. if your app rarely exceeds 200 tokens, you're in good shape.
[02:32] Tom Nguyen: our typical chat exchange is 120–180 tokens, but some serialized reports push into 500 tokens territory. we need graceful degradation.
[02:40] Carlos Ramirez: yep — routing policy we discussed earlier can send longer requests to a cheaper batch-optimized instance family, but that may increase latency. tradeoff there.
[02:48] Maya Patel: that's the usual latency vs cost tradeoff — can be tuned via routing policies and model variants. question — do you prefer a strict latency SLO or a cost budget?
[02:57] Priya Kapoor: product would prefer strict p95 latency band for UI flows, background tasks can be cost-optimized. so we want two classes.
[03:05] Maya Patel: great, we can map that to route: "realtime" vs "batch". we'll show configuration examples in the follow-up.
[03:12] Aaron Feld: one more security point — we need proof of SOC 2 Type II and logging retention policies (90/365 days). can we get a compliance matrix?
[03:20] Maya Patel: yes, we'll send the SOC 2 evidence summary and a retention options matrix. for hosted we keep event logs for 90 days standard; enterprise options extend that.
[03:28] Lena Cho: regarding the canary rollback, what's the default automatic fallback? do you have model variant fallback on error?
[03:33] Carlos Ramirez: we do. the platform can route to a downgraded compatible model or to an earlier pinned version automatically on increased error rate or latency. that's configurable.
[03:41] Tom Nguyen: about creds — we requested staging API keys, but the team needs read-only keys for developers. please make sure scopes are limited.
[03:48] Maya Patel: we'll provision a restricted API key set and a dev key. we'll also add IP allowlisting if you'd like.
[03:55] Priya Kapoor: yes IP allowlist for staging, and for production we want private deployment or dedicated.
[04:00] Maya Patel: noted — we'll present Dedicated/reserved capacity options in the pricing follow-up.
[04:05] Carlos Ramirez: quick note on throughput: in dedicated pools you'll see much better sustained throughput and more predictable tails. hosted is great for quick iteration.
[04:12] Lena Cho: timeline wise — we're aiming to have a small pilot live for internal users by Jan 10. any blockers to that?
[04:18] Tom Nguyen: peering and keys are blockers; once peering is done and we get keys we can run the smoke tests.
[04:24] Maya Patel: ok action items — tom finish peering, carlos run 2k bench, maya send security + SSO docs, aaron confirm KMS/HSM needs. Anything else?
[04:33] Aaron Feld: encryption in transit and at rest confirmation please — are you using TLS 1.3?
[04:37] Carlos Ramirez: yes TLS 1.3 for in-flight; at rest we use AES-256 and KMS for key management.
[04:43] Priya Kapoor: i want one more thing — can SE run a demo of the canary rollback behaviour with induced latency so we can see traces?
[04:50] Carlos Ramirez: sure we can simulate latency and show traces from the Redwood Console — we'll do a short demo in the next deep dive.
[04:56] Maya Patel: perfect. we'll schedule that with you. ok, quick bench detail i'll read out — carlos's 1k sample attached shows median 95ms, average 110ms, p95 210ms, p99 560 cold, warm p99 310.
[05:10] Tom Nguyen: those numbers are promising for our main flows. any known flakiness on tokens > 512?
[05:14] Carlos Ramirez: increased variance, yes. we recommend chunking or offloading to batch routes for very long sequences.
[05:21] Lena Cho: for our pilot, let's set the p95 target to 220ms for realtime, p99 under 500ms desirable.
[05:27] Maya Patel: jotting that down — p95 <= 220ms realtime. p99 < 500ms goal. we'll map monitoring alerts to the p95 threshold and escalate on p99 spikes.
[05:36] Priya Kapoor: who owns the alerting? is it in Redwood console or do we push to our datadog/splunk?
[05:41] Carlos Ramirez: both — we can push metrics to your datadog and set up alert hooks, and Redwood Console has native alerting too.
[05:47] Tom Nguyen: please provide the prometheus metrics names so we can wire them to our graphs.
[05:51] Maya Patel: will include a Prometheus -> Datadog mapping in the follow-up.
[05:56] Aaron Feld: also need to validate audit log formats for pipeline ingestion. can we send a sample event?
[06:01] Maya Patel: yes, we'll send a 10-event sample.
[06:04] Lena Cho: re: cost — what's the expected per-call cost for our mix? any rule of thumb?
[06:09] Carlos Ramirez: rough rule: short prompt, small model, hosted — lowest cost. adding quantization and batching reduces token compute cost by up to 30-40% in some workloads; Dedicated buys predictability more than raw per-token savings unless you're using reserved capacity. we'll model your mix after we get the request distribution.
[06:24] Priya Kapoor: ok that's fine. we'll send a CSV of sample requests to Carlos.
[06:28] Carlos Ramirez: thanks, that will let me produce a per-1k estimate.
[06:32] Maya Patel: timeline recap: we aim for internal pilot Jan 10, so key dates: peering resolved by 12/16-12/18, latency bench run by 12/17, security review week of 12/21.
[06:41] Tom Nguyen: peering being done tomorrow EOD is optimistic. i'll update.
[06:44] Maya Patel: great. any blockers we haven't covered?
[06:47] Priya Kapoor: none from product.
[06:49] Aaron Feld: one last: data residency. do you offer region locks for EU-only storage?
[06:54] Maya Patel: yes — hosted EU regions or private deployment ensures data residency. we'll call out region availability in the doc.
[06:59] Lena Cho: cool. thanks all.
[07:02] Maya Patel: okay we'll send notes and artifacts. carlos anything else?
[07:05] Carlos Ramirez: just to confirm i'll do the microbench and share traces and CSVs. also schedule the canary demo.
[07:11] Maya Patel: perfect. thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.

--- End Transcript ---
